correctness.rationale: For all m>=1, complex P and degree-m Q with boundary zeros, Q#=kappa Q follows from reciprocal-root invariance. The equality of boundary functions conjugate(phi)*Q^2=kappa^-1 Q P# makes T_conjugate(phi)(z^j Q^2) polynomial and places this polynomial in the domain of T_phi with product kappa^-1 z^j P P#. Adjointness and the standard de Branges–Rovnyak inner product establish the exact Gram-to-polynomial coefficient identity for every j,k>=0. Finite multiplication by Q(B_N)^2 reproduces those values in all rows j<=N-2m. The difference from the explicit upper Toeplitz band has only 2m potentially nonzero rows, proving the rank bound. Six Gaussian-integer examples and 726 entrywise comparisons were checked independently of the proof; computations are not used to infer the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The motivating arXiv:2603.03093v1 §4.3 only anticipates an all-order banded-plus-boundary phenomenon for one repeated boundary pole, and §4.2 proves its second-order case. It does not state/prove the explicit constant Toeplitz symbol or the arbitrary multiset of boundary poles. The accessible 2025 rational-space interpolation article and older higher-order Dirichlet descriptions address space geometry/interpolation or single-pole norms, not this finite Gram identity. Searches of the public mathematical literature and the searchable research index identified no theorem whose statement implies the present all-complex-coefficient finite band factorization. Prior Toeplitz norm identities are credited. Residual risk remains for unindexed or implicit prior equivalent formulas.

value.rationale: The motivating March 2026 work explicitly proposes a general all-order banded-Gram phenomenon as an expected next step, while its proved case is m=2 with one pole. This theorem resolves the all-order question with stronger, constant Toeplitz diagonals whose symbol is available directly from input polynomials, and extends to arbitrary configurations and multiplicities of boundary poles. It reduces the bulk Gram–Schmidt linear system to a fixed-band structure with a uniformly bounded boundary correction for each pole degree, a natural and reusable structural simplification rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
